Jordan / Karthik — taking the lead here. Attached is a first-pass sizing workbook and a 1-page SOW template (SOW highlights + optional burst clauses). Summary of the sizing pass:

- Recommended starting footprint (SG): 12 dedicated rA120 nodes (sustained target ~3.2k concurrent per node with batching & KV cache), which provides headroom for the 95th percentile daily spikes with expected latency SLAs.
- Warm EU fallback: 4 rA120 nodes kept warm (pre-warmed KV caches + queueing policy) to absorb ~20% overflow.
- US short-burst lane: use shared burst capacity with guaranteed minimum tokens during launch weeks (no dedicated nodes initially).
- Expected failover latency: 150–400ms additional routing + cache warm-up for cold keys (we recommend a short prefix caching strategy to reduce impact).
- Cost: estimate (monthly reserved + expected burst) included in the workbook — see tab "cost_estimate".

Attachments: redwood_sow_template_v1.pdf, nebula_capacity_estimates_v2.xlsx

Action items I propose:
1) Leah: confirm you can accept the suggested warm EU sizing and US burst approach.
2) Jordan/Karthik: approve SOW language and commit band ranges so procurement can review.

I can refine the workbook with per-hour queueing simulations if they want a tighter SLA/cost tradeoff.

— Irene
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference
